sections.heading: IBM’s existing strength
sections.content: When Gerstner took over IBM as it struggled with the microprocessor revolution, he saw that the company was respected and had relationships inside every large corporation—an asset he believed competitors lacked. IBM made that strength the basis of its approach: “embrace” and serve its customers. Rumelt presents those relationships as IBM’s source of power and leverage.
